questions.question: In pipelined processor microarchitecture, which of the following scenarios describes a structural hazard?
options: Two or more concurrent instructions require the same physical hardware resource in the same clock cycle due to resource constraints.
A subsequent instruction depends on the result of a preceding instruction that has not yet completed its writeback phase.
The instruction fetch unit cannot determine the next instruction address because a conditional branch target has not resolved.
An asynchronous external interrupt arrives, requiring the pipeline to immediately flush instructions and save state.
An instruction produces an arithmetic overflow that modifies status flags before a dependent instruction reads them.

questions.question: In modern high-performance processor front-ends, what is the primary architectural role of a Branch Target Buffer (BTB)?
options: To predict the directional outcome (taken vs. not-taken) of conditional branches using two-level adaptive history tables.
To provide the predicted target instruction address early in the fetch stage before the instruction is decoded.
To store and order completed branch instructions in program sequence until final retirement in the reorder buffer.
To track subroutine return addresses using a small, dedicated last-in-first-out (LIFO) circular hardware stack.
To perform translation of virtual instruction fetch addresses into physical addresses ahead of L1 cache access.

questions.question: In Static Timing Analysis (STA) of digital IC designs, what constitutes a 'false path'?
options: A timing path where the clock skew between source and destination registers exceeds the nominal clock cycle period.
A critical timing path that fails hold-time requirements exclusively under best-case fast-process voltage-temperature corners.
A topological path physically present in the gate netlist that cannot be functionally or logically sensitized during normal circuit operation.
A high-speed signal net that suffers severe propagation delay degradation due to capacitive crosstalk from adjacent aggressor wires.
An asynchronous reset distribution tree that inadvertently forms an open feedback loop during logic synthesis.

questions.question: In GPU architectures executing under the Single Instruction, Multiple Threads (SIMT) execution model, what fundamentally occurs when threads within a single warp encounter branch divergence?
options: The streaming multiprocessor automatically provisions extra compute cores to execute both branch paths concurrently at full hardware throughput.
The divergent warp is aborted and offloaded to the host CPU core to be resolved sequentially via speculative execution.
The thread occupying lane zero determines the execution path for the entire warp, permanently discarding the unselected path.
The divergent execution paths are executed serially, using thread active masks to disable inactive threads until the paths reconverge.
The warp transitions permanently from SIMT lock-step execution to independent out-of-order superscalar execution.

questions.question: In deep-submicron digital interconnect analysis, how does cross-coupling capacitance affect signal propagation delay when an aggressor net and a victim net switch simultaneously in opposite directions?
options: The effective coupling capacitance cancels to zero because the opposing voltage potentials neutralize the inter-wire electric field.
Inductive reactance overtakes capacitive coupling, accelerating signal slew and causing unexpected hold-time margins.
The effective coupling capacitance is halved, which shortens propagation delay and leads to potential signal undershoot.
Crosstalk between opposite-switching wires affects only dynamic power dissipation, leaving signal transition times unchanged.
The effective coupling capacitance increases due to the Miller effect, substantially increasing the victim net's propagation delay.
